citation.authors: Engmann L, Jin S, Sun F, Legro RS et al
citation.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology

record.population: 702 women with PCOS aged 18-40 wanting to conceive, in a US multicentre trial (non-Hispanic white, non-Hispanic black, Hispanic)
record.design: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial: insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome and androgen levels by group
record.finding: Non-Hispanic black women had a lower prevalence of metabolic syndrome than Hispanic women (24.5% against 42.2%) and lower triglycerides than Hispanic and white women. BMI and waist did not differ. The authors conclude non-Hispanic black women have an overall milder PCOS phenotype than Hispanics and in some respects than white women.
record.note: Women who wanted to conceive and entered a trial, so not a general population; the abstract shows no direct Black-against-white test on most outcomes.
